bc_asked_header: ## What you are asked to do
bc_asked_body:
Read the situation of each case and answer the questionnaire **with your own
professional judgement**, as you would in front of that equipment in the plant.
bc_rules_header: ## Three rules that make the exercise valid
bc_rule_1:
1. **Do not run the MIGRA-IA agent before you finish.** The aim is to
   compare your judgement against the program's; if you see the output first,
   the result no longer measures anything.
bc_rule_2:
2. **Do not consult the other co-authors until you hand it in.** What is
   measured is how much you agree independently.
bc_rule_3:
3. **If something cannot be known from what the case says, answer it as
   'Not known'.** Do not guess. Missing information is a valid result
   and the engine treats it as such.
bc_how_body:
Write the **number** of the option after the `=`, inside the back
quotes. For example: `` `M01 = 4` ``. You can also write the full text
of the option if you prefer.
bc_save_as: Save the file as `answers_YOURNAME.md` and return it.
bc_multi_note: _you can mark several, separated by a comma (e.g. 1,3)_
bc_note_f12: *(answer only if F01 = No or Not known)*
bc_key_note: Do NOT send this file to the co-authors: it maps each blind case to its id in the guide, which reveals the outcome.
bc_out_cases: Cases included, in the shuffled order:
bc_out_hidden: Hidden: full title, strategy, risks and tests of each case.
sr_intro1: Extracted automatically from `migra_ia/interactive.py` by `_scoring_rules.py`. If the code changes, this document changes.
sr_intro2: Each factor produces a value of 0-100 (higher = more risk). The total risk is the weighted mean of the eight, with the weights of Section 6.
sr_unknown: | *(not known)* | no default: see the notes |
sr_no_table: *No lookup table: the rule is conditional. See the notes.*
sr_tail_title: ## What these tables do not say
sr_tail: All these constants are set by hand, just like the weights. The sensitivity analysis of `_evaluation.py` perturbs **only the eight weights**, not these constants: the 100% stability it reports holds for the weighting, not for the rules. It is the next gap of the same family.
sr_note_estado_ciclo_vida: A direct table on M01. If M01 is 'Not known' the factor is NOT scored: it is omitted, the weights are renormalized and the gap is recorded as missing data. It is the only way for the engine not to assume a status that nobody declared.
sr_note_disponibilidad_repuestos: M04 sets the base. After that there is a CROSS-CHECK that the table does not show: the lead time (M06) is compared with the downtime the line tolerates (C10). If M06 is at 'From 2 to 8 weeks' or worse, the base is raised to a minimum of 85, because a spare part that arrives later than the plant can bear does not cover the risk on its own.
sr_note_soporte_fabricante: M09 (a current contract) sets the base and M07 (repair service) adjusts it up or down. If M09 is not known, the base stays at 55 unless M07 is not known either, in which case the factor is omitted.
sr_note_disponibilidad_software: ACCUMULATOR: it **starts at 20** and adds up the four tables above (N02 + N03 + N05 + N06). A value that is not listed adds the default indicated. The result is clamped to 0-100. The factor is only omitted if all four codes are missing at once.
sr_note_disponibilidad_respaldo:
A CASCADING CONDITIONAL, there is no table. It is evaluated in this order and stops at the first one that holds:

| Situation | Value |
|---|---|
| F01 was not answered | *factor omitted* |
| F01 = No (no copy exists) | 100 |
| F01 is not known | 90 |
| F06 = No (the backup does not open) | 100 |
| F07 = No (it does not compile) | 90 |
| F06 = Yes and F07 = Yes (verified) | 15 |
| incomplete verification | 70 |

The logic is Rule 3 of the guide: a backup that cannot be verified is treated as absent. That is why 'not known' (90) scores almost like 'does not exist' (100), and only a backup that opens AND compiles drops to 15.
sr_note_compatibilidad_sistemas:
ACCUMULATOR, there is no table. It **starts at 20** and adds for each thing the change drags along:

| Condition | Adds |
|---|---|
| G01 includes a proprietary network | +30 |
| G01 includes a network from an earlier generation* | +15 |
| O07 includes proprietary blocks | +20 |
| O07 includes an instruction list (AWL/STL) | +15 |
| O07 includes GRAFCET / SFC / GRAPH | +10 |
| O08 = Yes (proprietary libraries) | +25 |
| O02 = Yes (motion control) | +20 |

The two for G01 are mutually exclusive: proprietary takes precedence over legacy. Those for O07 accumulate with each other. It is clamped to 0-100.

*Networks considered to be from an earlier generation: MPI, Profibus DP, Profibus PA, DeviceNet, ControlNet, CC-Link, AS-Interface, RS-232, RS-485.
sr_note_historial_fallas:
L01 (the number of stoppages in 12 months) sets the step, which is a conditional and not a table:

| Stoppages in L01 | Value |
|---|---|
| 0 | 10 |
| 1 to 2 | 30 |
| 3 to 5 | 50 |
| more than 5 | 70 |
| no readable number | 45 |

On top of that step the L03 table above is added. Then a CAP is applied: if there is an uncorrected external root cause (a hot cabinet, poor grounding, a deficient power supply, a flat battery), the factor is **limited to 55**, because those faults are not attributable to the controller and replacing it does not correct them. It is the only factor whose value can GO DOWN because of a design rule.
sr_note_criticidad_productiva: C08 (criticality of the machine) sets the base; C10 (tolerable downtime) and Q04 (intervention window) raise it. If C08 is not known, the whole factor is omitted.

Generated by `_features.py` reading `%s` and
`%s`, which is itself extracted from the syntax
tree of the engine. If a factor stops reading a code, this document changes
by itself.
ft_decision:
Box 3 of the deliverable. The decision is taken and it is this one: **we do
not go with the raw data**. The project defines domain features -engineering
knowledge turned into a number- and weighs them; what follows says which
ones, with what weight, and which ones are collected and not used.
ft_candidates_title: ## The candidates of the field, against what the engine does
ft_factors_title: ## The eight factors of the engine and what they read
ft_factors_intro:
These are the ones that are implemented and weighted. The weights are the
ones of Section 6 of the paper and they are not touched without updating it.
ft_gaps_title: ## Gaps: what is collected and thrown away
ft_gaps_intro:
The questionnaire asks the technician for these data, stores them in the
case file and **no factor reads them**. It is the same class of defect as
F12, but on the two features the field names first:
ft_gaps_tail:
Closing it means touching `scoring.py`, whose eight factors and weights are
the ones the paper describes. It is an editorial decision, not a technical
one, and it is recorded as such.
ft_gaps_none: None: every candidate of the field feeds some factor.
ft_survivor_title: ## In the life-cycle table only one survives
ft_survivor:
The above is the questionnaire, which is where the domain knowledge of the
project lives. The tabular set on which the P1 baseline is trained is a
different one -`data/platform_lifecycle.csv`, nine platforms- and there the
leakage audit leaves **a single admissible variable: the age**. It is not a
modelling choice: the other columns either define the label or are metadata
of the collection process. See section 6 of
`%s`.
ft_survivor_tail:
Hence why enlarging the set is the task that unblocks the rest: as long
as the table has nine rows and one variable, the domain features are
defined but they cannot be exercised.
ft_cand_1_text: Year of manufacture and of installation. It is on the nameplate of the equipment and it predates any end-of-life event, so it cannot be contaminated by the label.
ft_cand_2_text: Year of end of support and of end of sale declared by the manufacturer. Both optional in the questionnaire: they are asked for 'if known'.
ft_cand_3_text: The one the domain calls for: it is the variable a plant manager already uses to decide.
ft_cand_4_text: Availability of a new spare part, of the secondary market and the lead time.
ft_cand_5_text: Networks the machine uses. It determines how much the change drags along.
ft_cand_6_text: Criticality of the machine, tolerable downtime and the cost of an hour stopped.

bl_rule_two_dates: (the first of two dates is taken)
bl_rule_ambiguous: AMBIGUOUS dd/mm vs mm/dd; day first is applied, like the rest of the table
bl_k_note: k=%d is the largest one with which every test fold has the %d classes. A larger k is impossible: only %d manufacturers contribute class %s, so there is nothing with which to fill more folds without splitting a brand.
bl_k_none: stratification was not possible: no k>=2 leaves both classes in every fold
bl_leak_identity: identity verified in %d of %d rows: %s = year(%s) - release. The date it is derived from is one of the dates that define the label, so the column is the label written another way.
bl_leak_dates: they are the columns from which the class is derived. Using them as a variable would be predicting the label with the label.
bl_leak_level: it measures how well verified the datum is against the source (A/B/C), not a property of the equipment. It is metadata of the collection process: if it got in, the model would learn the documentary habit of the manufacturer.
bl_leak_manufacturer: it is the grouping variable. In leave-one-manufacturer-out the test brand never appears in training, so as a variable it is unusable: it only serves to form the folds.
bl_leak_age: it predates any end-of-life event and it is available on the nameplate of the equipment. The only variable that survives the audit.
bl_title: REPRODUCIBLE BASELINE: ORDINAL RISK AND REPLACEMENT PRIORITY
bl_covered: Subproblem covered: P1 (ordinal risk). For P2 see section 7.
bl_origin: Origin    : Table 2 of the 'frequency table' (aggregated MEAN row excluded)
bl_classes: Classes   : %d present of the %d defined in the scale
bl_bias:
SELECTION BIAS, declared: the table was built to document
  discontinuations, so it only contains platforms that are already
  discontinued. There is not a single sample of classes 1 and 2. A
  classifier trained here cannot learn to recognize a current platform, and
  the ordinal model degenerates in practice into a binary one: with two
  classes only one cut is left.
bl_dates_title: Conversion of dates (to audit cell by cell):
bl_missing: Missing data: %d platforms with some date absent
bl_scheme:
Scheme    : stratified by obsolescence level, grouping by brand
              (the scheme assigned by the field)
bl_grouping:
Grouped by: Manufacturer. The field says "migration case" because it
              assumes components that share a case; here each row is an
              independent platform and there are no cases, so the unit
              that groups is the brand: they share a support policy.
bl_strat: Stratifies: each test fold contains both classes present.
bl_prep:
Preprocessing INSIDE the fold: the mean and the deviation with which the
  age is standardized are computed only with the training part of each
  fold, in b1_ordinal_logistic(). There is no fit made once over the nine
  rows.
bl_loo:
Contrast with leave-one-manufacturer-out (k=5), which groups but does NOT
  stratify: there the Mitsubishi fold comes out pure -its two platforms are
  class 4- and both models score 0.000 on it. That is exactly the
  distortion that stratification avoids.
bl_s34: 3 and 4. BASELINES, SAME SPLIT AND SAME METRICS
bl_b0: B0 trivial : majority class of the training fold. No variables.
bl_b1:
B1 classic : ordinal logistic regression (proportional odds)
               on the age, the model assigned by the field.
bl_b1_params: L2=%s, step=%s, iterations=%s, start at zeros.
bl_cv_title: RESULT OF THE CROSS-VALIDATION (mean +- deviation of the %d folds)
bl_main_metric:
MAIN METRIC, frozen by VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md point 3: macro F1.
  It is the one that decides. The accuracy and the ordinal error explain,
  they do not decide: with 6 samples of class 3 and 3 of class 4, the
  accuracy rewards whoever always says the majority class.
bl_dispersion:
The deviation is still large, and it has to be: with nine rows spread
  over few folds, one hit or one miss moves the figure of a whole fold.
  Reporting the mean without the deviation would hide that.
bl_micro_title: Pooling the 9 predictions into one bag (micro), as a contrast:
bl_coef_title: Coefficients per fold (this is what an engineer can audit):
bl_beta_note:
a positive beta = more age pushes towards higher classes, which is
     the expected direction. The slope is in units of the standard
     deviation of the age of the fold itself, not in years.
bl_reading_lose:
READING: the classic model does NOT beat the trivial one. With a single
  variable and nine rows it is an expected result, and it is the one that
  has to be published: it says that at this size the age on its own does
  not separate the classes better than counting which one is commonest.
bl_reading_win:
READING: the classic model beats the trivial one ON AVERAGE. The
  difference is NOT statistically sustainable: with folds of 1 and 2
  samples the deviation between folds is of the order of the difference
  itself, so the interval of one covers the mean of the other. It serves
  as an indication that the age carries signal, not as evidence that the
  model works.
bl_seed_use:
Actual use        : NONE. There is no stochastic step: the fit starts at
                      zeros, the step and the iterations are fixed and there
                      is no shuffling and no sampling. Reproducibility does
                      not depend on the seed, and that is why it is said
                      instead of suggesting that it does.
bl_deps: Dependencies of the computation: none from third parties (standard library)
bl_leak_result: RESULT: of the available columns, %d survives.
bl_leak_tail:
The set admits exactly one uncontaminated variable. That is the finding,
  and it conditions everything above: the classic model had no choice but
  to be univariate.
bl_bank:
Outside this table, in the case bank of the artifact:
     - The development scenarios 'critico' and 'otra_marca' share the same
       24 answers: they are 2 independent cases, not 3.
     - 'critico' (S7-300 -> S7-1500) reproduces the route of blind case 26.1,
       and the target of 'otra_marca' (Omron NX) that of blind case 26.5:
       the development set treads on the test set.
     - In agent mode with the API, the query_guide tool reaches
       data/<language>/knowledge_base.json, which contains the five blind
       cases with their strategy. In deterministic mode it does not:
       interactive.py does not import knowledge. The leak exists and it
       depends on the mode.
bl_holdout:
TEST SET SET ASIDE: the five case studies of the guide and the labels of
  the panel of experts are still UNOPENED. Everything above happens inside
  the development loop: they are %d validation folds over the nine
  platforms, not a measurement on data set aside.
bl_s7: 7. P2 REPLACEMENT PRIORITY - NOT EVALUABLE YET
bl_p2:
The classic model assigned to P2 is gradient boosting in ranking mode. It is
  not run, and the reason is not technical but one of data: a ranking model
  needs a reference ordering -which platform must be replaced before which-
  and that ordering does not exist in any source of the project.
bl_p2_circular:
Deriving it from the score of the engine itself would be circular: the
  model would learn to reproduce the formula it is meant to evaluate.
bl_p2_todo:
What is needed to unblock it, in order of cost:
     1. A priority ordering by expert judgement over these 9 platforms,
        issued by the co-authors without seeing the output of the engine. It
        is the same procedure as _blind_template.py and it can be asked for
        in one session.
     2. Enlarging the life-cycle table to the 130 generations of the
        catalog, which is what would give a set where boosting makes sense.
        Extraction and verification work on official sources.

t2_protocol:
# PROTOCOL — experimental configuration

**This paragraph is the experimental configuration section of the article.**
It replaces the protocol written as a separate document: it is pasted almost
literally into Overleaf, and what it says here rules over whatever the results
say afterwards.

Generated by `_table_ii.py`. No datum is written by hand: they come from running
`_baseline.py`, from measuring the times and from asking the system about the
machine. To update it the script is run again, this file is not edited.

The seven sentences cover, in order, what the guideline requires: data set
—source, size, classes and unit of observation—; split —proportions, grouping,
seed and the test set held out—; preprocessing and features —what is computed
and what is fitted inside each fold—; models compared —which ones, with library
and version—; hyperparameter search —space, criterion and the same effort for
all—; validation and metrics —scheme, *k*, repetitions, main and secondary—;
and hardware and reproducibility —machine, training time, seed and the link to
the repository—.
